newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Army commander Major General Rohan Daluwatte pledges to wipe out separatist Tamil rebels and pave way for peace. He was addressing the army's 47th anniversary celebrations in Colombo.
Sri Lanka's winning cricket coach Davenall Whatmore says his reasons for quitting the World Cup champions side are "personal and domestic".
Government asks retired army personnel to rejoin the force to guard Colombo and suburbs, which would enable the army to deploy more troops to the northeast where it is fighting Tamil rebels.
Tension high in eastern port town of Trincomalee following clashes between government troops and pro-government Tamil militiamen.
Sri Lankan successfully completes attempt to enter the Guiness Book of World Records by pulling two railway carriages weighing 120 tonnes, with his teeth at Colombo's Fort railway station.
Armed men rob a garment factory payroll worth one million rupees in broad daylight at Mahawa in the northcentral province. Two policemen guarding the cash and one of the robbers killed in the firing.
Twenty five main opposition United National Party members willing to go to northern Jaffna peninsula to observe rehabilitation, reconstruction work in former rebel stronghold.
Schools and shops closed in Trincomalee as tension mounts after clashes between government troops and pro-government Tamil militiamen.
Army commander Major General Rohan Daluwatte says his troops will fight to bring peace to the Indian Ocean island. He was addressing the army's 47th anniversary celebrations in Colombo.
